title: Five cops 'directly' involved in fatal shooting
article: As many as five Winnipeg police officers shot and fatally wounded a suspect on a field near the intersection of Grant Avenue and Kenaston Boulevard on Friday afternoon.
Police confirmed Saturday that Mark Dicesare, 24, of Winnipeg, succumbed to his wounds in hospital.

"At least 25 officers were involved in the incident," Deputy Chief Danny Smyth said. "Five officers have been identified as directly involved officers. What that means is that they were involved in the lethal-force encounter at the standoff in the field."

Witnesses told the Sun they'd heard at least six shots fired, but Smyth declined to specify the number, saying only that the incident is being investigated by the Independent Investigation Unit (IIU) of Manitoba. Although witnesses say they saw Dicesare waving a gun, Smyth could not confirm that either.
Police started to chase Dicesare after spotting him driving erratically in the Tuxedo area at about 12:20 p.m.

"Mr. Dicesare was in the vicinity of Ridgewood and Oakdale," Smyth said. "The officer focused her attention to Mr. Dicesare and his vehicle because of erratic behaviour and called for backup, and attempted to follow. Mr. Dicesare sped away and was lost for a period of time around the vicinity of Wilkes and Fairmont. Shortly afterwards, Mr. Dicesare's vehicle was observed in the area of Waverley and Taylor and what followed was a pursuit that went on for some time.

"The pursuit ended in the field just north of Grant Avenue at the intersection of Kenaston. Police units contained Mr. Dicesare in the field and attempted to engage with him. What followed was a standoff that lasted for approximately 20 minutes. The standoff ended when Mr. Dicesare took action that officers responded to with lethal force."
Police could not comment on a rumour that Dicesare had asked to speak to his mother before being shot.
Paramedics at the scene provided medical attention to Dicesare. No officers were injured.

The "directly involved" officers are now going through "a critical incident" process, Smyth said. That involves both forensic examination and a check on their well-being before they can return to duty.
Several of Dicesare's friends reacted on Twitter.
"It sucks you see someone 3 days ago and now there gone Rip Mark <3 you will be remembered," wrote @ChilnlikaDhilon.

Another Tweeter, who posted that her brother was friends with Dicesare, wrote, "police are willing to protect themselves more than they are willing to protect the people that they are SUPPOSED to protect."
